segments.note: Why, avoid[0] and prefer[1] retain the canonical-catalog rationale, component derivation, effort estimation, consistency with coder conventions and rejection of ad-hoc types or weights.

activation.note: Activation covers planner component derivation, URN side/layer selection, suffix selection, weight-based estimation and catalog maintenance. Excluding implementation alone respects the planner scope; task terms are contextual signals rather than independent obligations. Phase/change detection is explicitly unavailable without new observers, and cross-entry findings are honestly reviewer-judged.

audit.summary: All 275 segments survive at the claimed destinations, including every catalog suffix, description, weight, example and provenance field. The shared node contains genuinely reusable reference data rather than planner-specific obligations; the single-entry selection obligation stays in the rule, and elaborations are traceable or declared without adding waivers.

risks: The fields do not say what to do when no catalog description fits; a weak planner must infer that it should stop/flag rather than invent a type.
Correct lookup depends on the referenced shared catalog being supplied; the coder-facing fields themselves do not inline its entries.

unobservable: phase=planning requires a new observer for plan/WMBT/doc authoring activity
change to component side/layer/type/URN, file pattern, weight, or the catalog requires new diff-level observers
finding that values do not come from one matching entry, or that the catalog is incomplete/out of sync, is LLM-judged rather than a Datalog-observable fact

review.summary: Independent checks found the complete shared catalog intact, including all suffixes, descriptions, weights, missing-language cases, and examples; the auditor's compression judgment for S266 is also sound. The planner-facing fields clearly require single-entry lookup, though activation is not currently deterministic because phase/change observers and objective finding detection are absent. I agree with the PASS verdict.
